title: When Snap City occurs
summary: Following his video on where injuries occur (form and the red zone), NH covers when they occur: weight selection, accumulated fatigue and external stressors. Programming is the tool to manage the 'when', and with it bodybuilding should be injury-free for years.
claims: Early YouTube fitness focused injury prevention on form (the where); that remains correct but misses timing factors (the when)
The most obvious cause of injury is a weight too heavy for you, which compromises form
Saying there is no such thing as bad form wrongly implies weight selection plays no role in injury prevention
In bodybuilding form breakdown is not acceptable: the 10th rep must look as crisp as the first, only slower
Accumulated fatigue matters: weekly work done, how many leg days, lower back state, total volume
Programming is not only for planning progression; it also tracks past fatigue so you can prevent injury in the moment
Modern YouTube fitness does well in showing stress is a normal part of training; managing its accumulation is just as important
External factors such as focus, gym hassles and life stress may be the most important injury factor
For injuries like tendonitis, psychological stress may be the main factor, even more than form, because stress builds inflammation
On very stressful days his old tendonitis flares up without any change in training
The where and when of injury can't be understood without each other, just like volume and intensity
Form is awareness of the body in the moment; programming is awareness of the body over time
Injuries are never random; they are predictable when the where and when coincide, so they can be prevented
Bodybuilding is a safe practice: you should be able to train for 10 years with zero injuries
